entities.summary:
Sō Sadamori was a military commander of the early to mid-Muromachi period in Japan, serving as the shugo daimyō of Tsushima from 1423 to 1447. He played a pivotal role in the struggle for power among the daimyō of Japan during this tumultuous era.

Sō Sadamori's military campaigns were marked by his innovative use of firearms and his ability to adapt to changing circumstances on the battlefield. His leadership and strategic thinking were instrumental in the Sō clan's rise to prominence in the region.

The legacy of Sō Sadamori can be seen in the continued influence of the Sō clan in Japanese politics and society. His military campaigns also had a lasting impact on the development of Japanese warfare, with many of his tactics and strategies being studied by military leaders for centuries to come.

His death in 1452 marked the end of an era, but his impact on Japanese history continued to be felt for centuries to come.
